title: ProbMoE: Differentiable Probabilistic Routing for Mixture-of-Experts
claim: Conventional routing picks experts with a deterministic top-k and limited gradients; ours samples subsets probabilistically and gets informative router gradients.
layout: 2 panels side by side, shared input on top, legend bottom right
description: A shared 'Input x' box and a 'Router logits' box sit at the top and branch left and right. The left panel, 'CONVENTIONAL / Deterministic', is a vertical flow. Softmax probabilities (pink) feed a TopK box (cream). That box connects to three green expert boxes f1, f2 and f3, with f2 greyed out because it is not selected. The experts feed a weighted-sum box at the bottom. The right panel, 'ProbMoE / Probabilistic', shows softmax probabilities with a small bar chart. A purple box labelled S ~ P(S|B) samples a subset under a cardinality budget. The sampled subset feeds experts f1 to f3, which feed a sum box. A dashed yellow backward path labelled 'Straight-through marginal gradient estimator' returns to the router. Blue solid arrows show the forward pass and dashed yellow arrows show gradients. A legend at the bottom gives the colour key for the forward pass, gradient, expert and stochastic step.
caption: Comparison of conventional Top-$k$ training and ProbMoE training. Left: Conventional MoE applies a deterministic top-$k$ operator to the softmax routing probabilities for expert selection, while propagating gradients only through these probabilities. Right: ProbMoE models expert routing as probabilistic inference over discrete expert subsets. ProbMoE samples an expert subset $S$ from a cardinality-constrained distribution. Let $z$ denote the binary mask of the sampled subset and let $m$ denote the corresponding expert-selection marginals. Gradients are propagated through the straight-through mask $g=\operatorname{stopgrad}(z-m)+m$, which is combined with the softmax routing probabilities to form the final routing weights. This yields informative router gradients while preserving sparse expert execution. ProbMoE Dynamic-$k$ allows the subset size to vary within a range, with ProbMoE Exact-$k$ recovered as a special case.
abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models scale by activating only a small subset of experts per token. However, training such models remains challenging because top-$k$ routing is discrete and non-differentiable, requiring gradient estimators for expert selection whose design remains a central open problem. We introduce ProbMoE, a probabilistic routing framework that models expert selection as a distribution over cardinality-constrained expert subsets and formulates routing as probabilistic inference in this discrete subset space. We first propose ProbMoE Exact-$k$ routing, which samples $k$-expert subsets in the forward pass, and the backward pass uses gradients through each expert's exact marginal probability as a tractable surrogate for the true gradient. ProbMoE naturally generalizes to a dynamic-$k$ routing setting, where both training and inference constrain the routing cardinality to the same predefined range, allowing adaptive expert allocation per token. Across benchmarks and model backbones, ProbMoE Exact-$k$ achieves strong performance compared to competitive baselines, with improved expert utilization and routing diversity; ProbMoE Dynamic-$k$ achieves comparable performance with fewer activated experts.
